book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: Expression adopted by sherpa?

definitions.meaning: the surface reading: a saying a mountain guide might use
the setter's reading: rearrange the letters of 'phrase' and you get sherpa, so the guide's name is itself a reworking of a word for a form of words

explanation.surface: A Himalayan guide picks up a favourite saying on the trek.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a reverse trick: SHERPA is an anagram, a 'turn', of PHRASE, so the word sherpa is literally a TURN OF PHRASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn of phrase is an idiom for a particular way of putting something into words.

clue.text: Volatile voter accepting popular figure on course

indicators.note: accepting means the rearranged voter takes popular in
volatile means unstable, liable to change, so the letters of voter change order

parts.note: the word voter itself supplies the letters to be rearranged
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A fickle elector backs a well-liked racecourse personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests horse racing, but it is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee Trevino is a famous Mexican-American professional golfer, a figure on the golf course.

clue.text: Dutch club to get on natural protection?

parts.note: Dutch is slang for wife (my old Dutch), and so is rib, from Adam's rib
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards
to age is to get on in years

explanation.surface: A football club from the Netherlands gets a natural shield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch club' looks like Ajax or PSV; it is two pieces, a slang word for wife and the card-suit letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The ribcage is the bony structure that shields the heart and lungs, protection built into the body.

clue.text: Gold box by artist? It's found in pit

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a chest is a large box
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A miner finds a gold casket and a painting down a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pit' suggests a mine; it is the orchestra pit below the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre musicians play in the orchestra pit, a sunken area in front of the stage.

clue.text: Genuine Shakespearean character acting

parts.note: Puck is the mischievous sprite in A Midsummer Night's Dream
A is an abbreviation for acting, as in an acting rank

explanation.surface: A true Shakespeare role being performed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pucka is a variant spelling of pukka, Anglo-Indian slang for authentic or proper.

clue.text: Lecture about to be taken by senior academic? Nothing in it

indicators.note: to be taken by places the first piece ahead of the academic, led by them

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: in it means the nothing goes inside the academic's word

parts.note: prof is short for professor
O, a zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A professor is about to give a lecture with nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lecture' looks like a university talk; here it is a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a scolding, and to give someone a lecture is to rebuke them at length.

clue.text: Casual journalist missing right device used by police

indicators.note: missing means the right is left out

parts.note: a stringer is a freelance journalist paid per piece

explanation.surface: A freelance reporter misses the right gadget the police are using.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinger is a spiked strip police lay across a road to puncture a fleeing car's tyres.

clue.text: A titled woman penned by Frenchman, book with a creative part?

parts.note: madame is the French form of address for a married woman
the ovary is the organ that produces eggs, a part involved in creating life

explanation.surface: A noblewoman written by a French author appears in a book with a creative role.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the novel itself, written by the Frenchman Gustave Flaubert.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame Bovary is the 1857 novel written by Gustave Flaubert, the French author.

clue.text: Bill facing fine about book is bitter

indicators.note: facing puts the bill up front, ahead of the rest

parts.note: an account, abbreviated AC, is a bill

indicators.note: about means the fine's letters go round the book

parts.note: an eric was a fine paid for a killing under old Irish law

explanation.surface: Someone sour about being handed a bill and a fine over a library book.
explanation.walkthrough: ERIC is an obscure dictionary word: in early Irish law, the blood-money paid by a killer to the victim's family.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbic is a synonym of bitter, as in a harsh, sharp-tongued remark.

clue.text: Manage to retain photo showing small trees

indicators.note: to retain means the managing word holds the picture inside it

parts.note: to cope is to manage
a pic is a photo

explanation.surface: A photographer gets by holding onto a picture of a little woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: A coppice is a thicket of small trees cut back periodically for regrowth.

clue.text: Commercial figure with energy and salesman, Gallic chap, in unusual turn

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: in places the salesman and the Frenchman inside the rearranged turn
unusual means the letters of turn appear in an odd order

parts.note: the word turn itself supplies the letters to be rearranged
a rep is a sales representative
Rene is a French man's name

explanation.surface: A lively ad star and a French salesman perform an odd routine.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepreneur is a person in business who starts ventures, a figure in commerce.

clue.text: A time in a French farmhouse causing stir

indicators.note: in places the first two pieces inside the farmhouse

parts.note: taken as written
a gite is a French country house, often let to holidaymakers
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stay at a holiday cottage in France causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate a liquid is to stir or shake it; also to cause a stir politically.

clue.text: In the midst of anxiety, keeping hold of doctor

indicators.note: keeping hold of means the anxiety word grips the doctor inside it

parts.note: angst is anxiety or dread
MO is a medical officer, a military doctor

explanation.surface: A worried patient clutches the GP's hand in the middle of a panic attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Amongst is a preposition meaning surrounded by or among, the same sense as in the midst of.

clue.text: Bolt blocking hostel opened

indicators.note: blocking suggests something sitting inside and across the words that follow, here spanning the two words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of hostel and the start of opened

explanation.surface: A door bolt jams a youth hostel's door that had been opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' reads as a door fastening, but it is the verb: to run off.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly to marry, so it means to bolt.

clue.text: Exotic fare cost around a grand for working party

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the grand
exotic means unusual or strange, so these letters come out in an unusual order

parts.note: the words fare and cost supply the letters to be rearranged
K, short for kilo, is slang for a thousand pounds, a grand

explanation.surface: Fancy food for a committee costs about a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a group set up to work on a specific problem, which is a working party.

clue.text: Show report of tiny spot with light touch

indicators.note: report means what is heard, so the two words are said and the sound gives the entry

parts.note: a speck is a tiny spot and a tickle is a light touch; said together, speck-tickle

explanation.surface: A news item about a small mark and a gentle pat.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking display or performance put on for viewers.

clue.text: Self-promotional side in field getting edge in money gained

parts.note: the on side is one half of a cricket field

indicators.note: in means the edge sits inside the takings

parts.note: the take is the money a business or show brings in
a hem is the edge of a garment

explanation.surface: A pushy cricketer fielding on the boundary earns money from it.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: On the make describes someone ambitiously seeking profit or advancement for themselves.

clue.text: Team excited about largely refined foreign dish

indicators.note: about means the rearranged team goes round the refined word
excited means stirred up, so the letters of team are jumbled

parts.note: the word team itself supplies the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: pure means refined, free of impurities

explanation.surface: A side gets excited about a fancy foreign meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is a Japanese dish of seafood or vegetables fried in light batter.

clue.text: Boiling egg initially with new recipe — and old?

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of egg

parts.note: the word whose opening letter is taken
R, from Latin recipe, the doctor's prescription mark
aged means old

explanation.surface: Cooking an egg with a fresh recipe, and whether to use an old one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boiling' sits beside the egg as cooking, but it means furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiling here means seething with anger, so enraged is a synonym.

clue.text: Drink remains by fire lacking note

indicators.note: lacking means the note is dropped from the remains

parts.note: a cinder is what is left of burnt fuel in a grate
N, for note, as in a banknote

explanation.surface: Someone drinks the dregs while sitting by a fire with no music.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is an alcoholic drink made from fermented apples.

clue.text: Priest, one protected by sect, is figure to blame

indicators.note: protected by means the sect wraps round the priest and the one

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A priest shielded by a sect is the one to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is the person responsible for a wrongdoing, the one at fault.

clue.text: Daughter found on river a small amount

indicators.note: found on, in a down clue, puts the daughter on top of the river

parts.note: the Ribble is a river in Lancashire, north-west England

explanation.surface: A daughter discovered on a river, with just a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A dribble is a trickle, a small quantity of liquid.

clue.text: Authority in the main a young chap backed around community

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: around means the reversed lad wraps the community
backed means the young chap's word is read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a young chap
a mir was a Russian peasant commune

explanation.surface: In the bulk of it, a youngster with authority over a community gets support.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old poetic word for the open sea, so authority there is a naval commander.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a top-ranking naval officer, one with command at sea.

clue.text: Old actress learning latest part on screen

parts.note: lore is learning or traditional knowledge

indicators.note: latest part means the final letter of screen

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A veteran actress learning her newest film role.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophia Loren is an Italian film star of the 1950s and 60s, a classic screen actress.

clue.text: Writer recalling much knowledge about India

indicators.note: recalling, calling back, signals that the word for much is read backwards

parts.note: a lot is much

indicators.note: about means the knowledge goes round the India

parts.note: ken is range of knowledge, as in beyond one's ken
India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An author recalls a great deal of what they know about India.
explanation.definitionFit: J. R. R. Tolkien was the English novelist who wrote The Lord of the Rings.

clue.text: Less grey university? No grey broadcast about it

indicators.note: about it means the rearranged letters go round the university
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the words no and grey supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A college that is less dull, with nothing drab in its broadcasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grey' looks like a dull colour; the definition means having fewer grey hairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Being younger generally means having less grey hair, so less grey stands for more youthful.

clue.text: Native American or French detected reindeer

parts.note: the Carib are an indigenous people of the Caribbean and northern South America
ou is French for or

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a reindeer, either Native American or French.
explanation.definitionFit: Caribou is the North American name for the reindeer, the same deer species.

clue.text: Green trade discharged with tips for cultivation — here?

definitions.text: Green trade discharged with tips for cultivation — here?

indicators.note: discharged means let off or released, so these letters are set loose and rearranged

parts.note: the words green and trade supply most of the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: tips are the two ends, so the first and last letters of cultivation

parts.note: the word whose first and last letters are added to the mix

explanation.surface: Where the horticultural trade is carried on, with advice on growing things.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a shop where green trade happens and gardening tips are given.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden centre is a retail business selling plants, seeds and gardening equipment.
